dial.summary: BTC surged to $77,416 on August 22 — up 22% on the week (biggest weekly rally in 3 years, best since March 2024) — with BTC dominance firming to 59.3% and total crypto rising to $2.64T; crucially, funding rates remain controlled and sentiment stays cautious-not-euphoric, reinforcing the accumulation character of the move; macro backdrop constructive: ISM at 55.6 (expansion), 2s10s steepening to +51bps, DXY neutral at 98.84 — only real yields (2.35%) remain a structural headwind; the decisive PCE/GDP/Warsh-keynote cluster (August 26–28) is the next macro gate before FOMC September 15–16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) carried at ~$102.7T — July aggregate not yet published (~6-week reporting lag); US M2 confirmed at $23.16T for June 2026, +5.6% YoY (record high, 28th consecutive monthly increase); no YoY contraction signal from any major central bank; 4-week trend up based on sustained US M2 expansion and continued global central bank balance sheet stability; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY contraction headwind condition not triggered).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading — August 2026 data releases September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8% (first factory hiring expansion in 18 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July reading is the highest since May 2022; 4-week trend up: June 53.3% → July 55.6% = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 98.84 on August 22, 2026 (up 0.06% on the day; essentially flat vs August 21 close of 98.86); 4-week trend down: DXY was ~101.2 around July 21 → 98.84 on August 22 = approximately -2.3%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury's expanded long-term buyback program; status NEUTRAL (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; a sustained close below 97.5 would flip to supportive; PCE August 26 and Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 are key directional catalysts).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.35% as of August 19, 2026 (most recent confirmed reading; nominal 10Y on August 21 = 4.71%, breakeven T10YIE = 2.30%); 10Y yield on August 22 traded around 4.70%, leaving real yield approximately unchanged at ~2.35%; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (July 21) → 2.35% (August 19) = +17bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold; a soft PCE on August 26 and dovish Warsh keynote August 28 are the catalysts needed to compress real yields meaningfully below 2%).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 22, 2026: 10Y yield ~4.70% (latest intraday; August 21 FRED close 4.71%); DGS2 at 4.19% (last confirmed August 20); spread = +51bps; 4-week trend up: ~+35bps (July 21) → +51bps (August 22) = +16bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening trend intact; BTC rally to $77K+ and risk-on tone not pressuring the curve; PCE August 26 and Warsh tone August 28 are the next key curve inputs).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.76T for week ending August 12, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 13); week ending August 19 data (H.4.1 released August 20) consistent with prior week at ~$6.76T; 4-week trend flat: $6.70T (August 5) → $6.76T (August 12) = +$60B (+0.9% over 8 days; longer 4-week window approximately flat within 0.5% threshold); balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal; status supportive.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate carried at last confirmed reading of +0.0025%/8h; on August 22 BTC surged to $77,416 (+6.5% 24h, +22% weekly — biggest weekly rally in 3 years); multiple sources confirm funding remains 'controlled' and sentiment 'cautious-not-euphoric' despite the price surge, meaning the rally is driven by spot ETF inflows ($517M), short liquidations, and institutional demand rather than leveraged retail — this is the most credible accumulation signal; well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; 30-day trend down vs late-June/early-July levels; CoinGlass direct fetch blocked, funding rate value unchanged from prior confirmed reading.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (CoinGecko, August 22) vs total crypto market cap ~$2.64T (August 22, with BTC at $77,416 and BTC dominance at 59.3%); stablecoin dominance ~11.0%-11.6% (CoinGecko stated 11.04% share); 30-day trend down: ~14.3% (mid-July) → ~12.5% (August 21) → ~11.0% (August 22) — compressed as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets, particularly accelerating during this week's BTC rally; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL rises — is opposite of current dynamics).

upcoming.title: Consumer Confidence (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — first consumer sentiment read incorporating July NFP shock (−23K), hot core CPI (3.1%), FOMC Minutes (August 19), Flash PMI (August 21), and BTC's 22% weekly surge to $77,416 (biggest weekly rally in 3 years as of August 22); a sharp deterioration in confidence would raise Q3 recession risk and bolster the case for September rate cuts; precedes the decisive PCE/GDP cluster the following morning.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays at 8:30 AM ET — July PCE Price Index (Fed's preferred inflation gauge), Personal Income, and Personal Spending; arrives one day before Jackson Hole opens; hot core CPI (3.1% YoY, August 12) implies core PCE potentially 2.7–2.8% YoY; a reading above 2.8% strongly supports a September hike; a soft print (<2.5%) preserves the rate-cut path, reinforces BTC Accumulation, and could push DXY below 97.5 from current 98.84 — the single most important data print ahead of Jackson Hole.

upcoming.title: GDP 2nd Estimate (Q2 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA releases the second estimate of Q2 2026 GDP at 8:30 AM ET alongside July PCE, one day before Jackson Hole opens; July NFP shock (−23K) and hot core CPI (3.1%) have raised Q3 recession concerns; significant downward revisions alongside soft labor and hot inflation would reinforce the stagflation narrative and set the tone for Warsh's keynote the following morning.

upcoming.title: Jackson Hole Economic Symposium Opens (August 27–29)
upcoming.note: Kansas City Fed annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium begins at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming — runs August 27–29 (Thursday–Saturday); theme: 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy'; by the time proceedings open, markets will have processed PCE (August 26), GDP Q2 2nd estimate (August 26), Consumer Confidence (August 25), and BTC's historic 22% weekly rally; Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday morning August 28; FOMC September 15–16 is the next binding commitment.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 22, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 22, 2026 — released the opening morning of Jackson Hole; a sustained rise in claims arriving as Jackson Hole opens would immediately shape the tone for Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural keynote the next morning (August 28); context: July NFP shocked at −23K, making weekly claims particularly closely watched.

upcoming.title: Fed Chair Warsh Inaugural Jackson Hole Keynote
upcoming.note: Kevin Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole address Friday morning August 28 — the single most important macro event of this cycle for the crypto risk framework; by August 28 all macro inputs will be in hand (PCE August 26, GDP 2nd estimate August 26, Consumer Confidence August 25, Flash PMI August 21); a hawkish tone signaling September hike despite soft growth would sharply pressure risk assets; a neutral or dovish tone alongside soft PCE would be the macro green light to extend BTC's rally (currently $77,416) toward new all-time highs; could push DXY below 97.5 from current 98.84; September 15–16 FOMC is the next binding commitment.
